In Panama’s Pacific coastal zone during the height of the rainy season, persistent cloud cover, high atmospheric moisture, and frequent afternoon convection tied to the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) act as the dominant cooling mechanisms. These factors typically cap daytime heating near 30–31 °C by reducing incoming solar radiation and triggering evaporative cooling from showers. Model guidance and recent analogs show only modest day-to-day variability (±1–2 °C) under prevailing trade-wind and sea-breeze regimes, which explains why outcomes outside 29–32 °C carry sharply lower probabilities.  

Slightly higher odds on 31 °C versus 30 °C reflect the possibility of marginally clearer morning skies or a delayed shower onset allowing brief additional insolation, while 32 °C+ remains a low-probability outlier requiring unusually suppressed convection. eventMetadata.context_description: **Latest forecast guidance from models and agencies like the China Meteorological Administration points to a peak temperature in the upper 30s Celsius for Chengdu on July 22, 2026, amid the influence of the Western Pacific Subtropical High.** This ridge typically sustains hot, subsiding air over the Sichuan Basin during peak summer, amplified by the urban heat island effect and high humidity that limits nighttime cooling. Recent model runs show modest variability, with some projecting 38–39°C under partly cloudy conditions and others allowing brief excursions toward 40–41°C if subsidence strengthens or winds remain light. Incoming moisture or a weak frontal boundary could cap readings near 37–38°C. Trader consensus clusters tightly around 39–41°C because these thresholds align with ensemble spreads and historical July extremes, while probabilities drop sharply outside this window as resolution nears. Updated model outputs expected within 24–48 hours will likely refine the outcome.

**Trader sentiment for Austin’s July 22 high temperature centers on a strong ridge of high pressure promoting clear skies, strong daytime heating, and minimal cloud cover or precipitation.** Official National Weather Service forecasts and National Blend of Models guidance issued around July 20 point to highs near 99–101 °F for the immediate period, with the warmest day of the week expected mid-week. This setup favors the closely matched leading bins of 102–103 °F (36 %) and 104–105 °F (33.5 %), reflecting small but meaningful differences in model timing of any weak moisture return or slight wind shifts that could trim or enhance peak heating by a degree or two.

Key scientific variables include surface dew points in the mid-70s, which elevate heat-index values but also limit extreme surface warming through modest evaporative cooling; light south-to-southeast winds that maintain downslope warming without strong advection of cooler air; and the absence of organized convection or frontal passages that would otherwise increase cloud cover. Historical July climatology for Austin (normal high ~97 °F) places these outcomes well above average, consistent with the current ridge pattern. Resolution hinges on the official 24-hour maximum recorded at approved stations on July 22; any last-minute model shift toward slightly higher or lower insolation could readily tip the narrow gap between the two leading outcomes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Jul '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent meteorological forecasts for Karachi indicate persistent monsoon-related cloud cover, light showers, and elevated humidity moderating daytime highs near 31–32°C through July 23, consistent with July climatology where averages peak around 31°C. Arabian Sea breezes and high moisture content limit extreme heating, though model spreads allow for brief clearing that could push readings to 33–34°C. Trader consensus clustering on 34°C as the mode reflects this variability and recent observations of slightly above-average warmth amid patchy rain, while lower probabilities on 35°C+ or sub-32°C outcomes align with official guidance from regional agencies showing limited intensification potential before resolution.
